overview.title: What is OASA?
overview.text: OASA is a regenerative village network that transitions land from extractive ownership into perpetual community commons managed for long-term ecological health.

overview.title: Who joins OASA?
overview.text: The community draws land stewards, creatives, remote workers, families, systems thinkers, and nature lovers who want to live in closer relationship with the land. Most members engage through [Traditional Dream Factory](https://traditionaldreamfactory.com) (TDF), the first active OASA node, situated on 25 hectares in Portugal's Alentejo region. Participation ranges from short-stay visits and two-week volunteer programs to long-term co-housing arrangements.

overview.title: The OASA Token Model
overview.text: OASA uses a utility token system where one $TDF token grants one night of annual accommodation and one governance vote at [Traditional Dream Factory](https://traditionaldreamfactory.com/token). Members hold use rights rather than speculative land ownership, and all token proceeds fund ecological restoration and community infrastructure. As of May 2026, there were 288 token holders with tokens priced at EUR 262 each.

history.text:
OASA was founded in 2021 when Franco-Danish entrepreneur [Samuel Delesque](https://traditionaldreamfactory.com/team) converted a former poultry factory in Portugal's Alentejo into a regenerative village called Traditional Dream Factory. The OASA Association was formally registered as a Swiss non-profit in Zug, one of the few jurisdictions providing a legal home for DAO-structured organizations.

In 2023, TDF launched its $TDF token platform, enabling community members to hold perpetual accommodation rights and governance votes without speculative land ownership. Early fundraising brought in EUR 384k through token sales alongside private investment rounds totaling EUR 800k. By 2025, the community had grown to 288 token holders, harvested 1.2 million litres of rainwater, and planted over 4,000 trees across the property.

OASA is designed to replicate as a network: new projects can apply to join, subject to ecological review and approval by the OASA General Meeting. The 2025 OASA Constitution sets binding standards for soil health, water capture, biodiversity, and community governance that every node must maintain.

location:
OASA's first and currently active node, [Traditional Dream Factory](https://traditionaldreamfactory.com) (TDF), occupies 25 hectares in the Alentejo region of southern Portugal, roughly two hours from Lisbon by road. The land follows OASA's ecological principles: 50% is designated as a wild rewilding core, 45% is under syntropic agroforestry with 65-plus tree species, and less than 5% is built infrastructure.

The OASA Association is registered as a non-profit in Zug, Switzerland, which provides a legal framework for the DAO governance structure. Physical community life, work, and activities happen on the Portuguese property.

The Alentejo climate is mild and dry, suited to year-round habitation. By 2025, the village had documented 40-plus bird species on the property, including species not recorded in the area for decades, and recharged previously dried local wells.
duration:
Stays at OASA's TDF village range from short visits to permanent co-housing. Volunteers commit to a minimum of two weeks (one month recommended), contributing four hours of work per day in exchange for shared dormitory accommodation, with programs starting on Sundays.

Nomad residency programs run monthly - the [Nomad May](https://traditionaldreamfactory.com/stay) program, for example, runs May 1-31 and includes workshops, community dinners, and scheduled activities. Standard bookable stays are available through the [TDF booking engine](https://traditionaldreamfactory.com/stay) year-round.

Token holders at citizenship level (30 tokens minimum) receive one night of annual accommodation per token held, with no prescribed maximum stay enforced by the token model. Co-housing residents sign a 7-year renewable contract with a minimum presence of three months per two-year period.
pricing:
OASA's primary access model is the $TDF utility token, priced at EUR 262 per token as of May 2026. One token grants one night of annual accommodation (at the standard room tier) plus one governance vote in the DAO. Accommodation costs differ by type: budget options such as camping use 0.5 tokens per night, while premium suites may use up to 5 tokens per night.

Token tiers:
- 1 token (EUR 262): one annual night + one governance vote
- 10 tokens (EUR 2,620): 10 annual nights + complimentary weekend + voting rights
- 30 tokens (EUR 7,860): full citizenship - 30 annual nights, instant booking priority, plus a permaculture course

Monthly residency programs run EUR 320-EUR 1,130 per month depending on accommodation type (Nomad May 2026 pricing). Pre-booked 30-day stays are available at approximately EUR 900 per month. Volunteering requires no token purchase; volunteers receive shared dormitory accommodation in exchange for four hours of daily work.

Co-housing units (planned delivery 2027-2028): [Earthpods](https://traditionaldreamfactory.com/cohousing) (50-90 m², 10 units) from 365 tokens locked; Townhouses (144 m², 13 units) from 750 tokens locked. Monthly utility contributions for co-housing residents run EUR 150-250.

longtermer:
TDF's co-housing program, [Dream Neighbors](https://traditionaldreamfactory.com/cohousing), offers a path to permanent residency for members ready to commit long-term. Two home types are available: Earthpods (50-90 m², 10 units, from 365 tokens locked) and Townhouses (144 m², 13 units, from 750 tokens locked). Both include full shared access to the restaurant, bio-pool, sauna, coworking, and makerspace, plus subletting rights with 50% revenue retained by the homeowner.

Co-housing residents sign a 7-year renewable contract, commit to a minimum three months on-site per two-year period, and contribute four hours per week of community work. Monthly utility contributions run EUR 150-250. Construction is planned in phases, with delivery targeted for 2027-2028 as capital milestones are met.

Prospective co-housing residents complete intake screening and a detailed application process after joining the waitlist at [traditionaldreamfactory.com/cohousing](https://traditionaldreamfactory.com/cohousing).

howToEnter.text:
The most direct way to join the OASA community is to [purchase $TDF tokens](https://traditionaldreamfactory.com/token) at EUR 262 each. One token grants one annual night of accommodation and one governance vote; 30 tokens qualifies a member for citizenship with instant booking privileges and a permaculture course.

Short and monthly stays can be booked through [the TDF booking engine](https://traditionaldreamfactory.com/stay) without token ownership. Nomad residency programs like Nomad May offer structured month-long stays with workshops and community activities included.

Volunteers can apply by emailing [space@traditionaldreamfactory.com](mailto:space@traditionaldreamfactory.com), committing to a minimum two-week stay with four hours of daily community work. Those interested in permanent co-housing can join the waitlist at [traditionaldreamfactory.com/cohousing](https://traditionaldreamfactory.com/cohousing).

faqs.question: What is OASA?
faqs.answer: OASA is a regenerative village network and legal framework that transitions privately held land into perpetual community commons. Members hold utility tokens representing access rights and governance votes rather than land ownership. The first active OASA node is [Traditional Dream Factory](https://traditionaldreamfactory.com) in Portugal's Alentejo region, founded in 2021.

faqs.question: Where is the OASA village located?
faqs.answer: The active OASA village is Traditional Dream Factory (TDF), located on 25 hectares in the Alentejo region of southern Portugal, approximately two hours from Lisbon. The OASA Association is registered as a non-profit in Zug, Switzerland, which provides the legal framework for the DAO governance structure.

faqs.question: How does the OASA token model work?
faqs.answer: Each $TDF token grants one night of annual accommodation at TDF and one vote in the community DAO. Tokens are sold at a bonding-curve price (EUR 262 as of May 2026) and represent perpetual access rights - not equity, not land ownership. Tokens cannot be redeemed by the treasury, which prevents speculative dynamics. You can [buy tokens here](https://traditionaldreamfactory.com/token).

faqs.question: What does OASA citizenship require?
faqs.answer: A minimum of 30 $TDF tokens qualifies a member for citizenship, which provides instant booking privileges, 30 annual accommodation nights, and full governance participation. Citizens must also have contributed materially to stewardship and be vouched for by existing community members. The cost of 30 tokens is approximately EUR 7,860 at the May 2026 token price.

faqs.question: How do I book a stay at TDF?
faqs.answer: Short and monthly stays are bookable through [the TDF booking engine](https://traditionaldreamfactory.com/stay). Structured month-long residency programs like Nomad May (EUR 320-EUR 1,130 per month) are announced on the TDF website. Pre-booked 30-day stays are also available at approximately EUR 900 per month.

faqs.question: Can I volunteer at OASA without buying tokens?
faqs.answer: Yes. Volunteers commit to a minimum of two weeks (one month recommended), contributing four hours of daily work in areas such as regenerative gardening, hospitality, kitchen support, construction, and mushroom cultivation. Volunteers receive shared dormitory accommodation and home-cooked vegetarian meals. Apply by emailing space@traditionaldreamfactory.com.

faqs.question: What regenerative practices does OASA follow?
faqs.answer: OASA enforces seven ecological principles across all nodes: Soil (living plant cover, no synthetic inputs), Water (rainwater capture, minimal aquifer use), Air (no toxic burning, active carbon sequestration), Waste (composting, recycling, no dumping), Biodiversity (50%+ land rewilded, minimum 20 species per hectare), Resources (renewable energy, natural building materials), and Community (consent-based governance, open knowledge sharing). All OASA members must adhere to these principles.

faqs.question: Is OASA suitable for families?
faqs.answer: TDF actively attracts families as part of its community mix. The first child was born at TDF in September 2025. The village includes family-sized accommodation options including a 3-bedroom house and co-housing Townhouses with 3-4 bedrooms. Families interested in long-term co-housing can join the [Dream Neighbors waitlist](https://traditionaldreamfactory.com/cohousing).

faqs.question: What is the co-housing program?
faqs.answer: The [Dream Neighbors program](https://traditionaldreamfactory.com/cohousing) offers 23 private homes in two types: Earthpods (50-90 m², 10 units, from 365 tokens locked) and Townhouses (144 m², 13 units, from 750 tokens locked). Residents sign a 7-year renewable contract, commit to at least 3 months on-site per 2-year period, and contribute 4 hours of community work per week. Monthly utilities run EUR 150-250. Delivery is targeted for 2027-2028.

faqs.question: How is OASA structured legally?
faqs.answer: OASA is organized as a Swiss non-profit association registered in Zug, which provides a legal framework for DAO-structured organizations. Each OASA project operates through a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) or trust that holds land in commons. Land cannot be sold or speculated on, and all surpluses must be reinvested into ecological restoration or community wellbeing. No dividends or profit distributions are permitted.

faqs.question: How established is OASA?
faqs.answer: OASA and Traditional Dream Factory have been operating since 2021. By May 2026 the community had 288 token holders, had published annual transparency reports for 2021-2025, stored 1.2 million litres of rainwater, planted 4,000-plus trees, and documented 40-plus bird species on the property. The project has been covered by Reuters, Expresso, Diario de Noticias, and The Portugal News.
